title: Move _decodePayload() calls inside outbox_processor.dart's per-row try blocks so one bad payload can't abort the whole drain

evidence.quote:
// Continue draining other rows — don't abort the whole batch on
          // a single failure.

why: _decodePayload throws FormatException when a row's payload isn't a JSON object (DB corruption, a future write bug, or jsonEncode(null)). Both call sites sit OUTSIDE any try/catch: line 292 is inside the eligibleCompletions loop before the try at line 306, and line 383 is immediately before the per-row try at line 384. A single malformed row therefore throws all the way out of _drainForProfile → _doDrain → drain()'s try/finally (the finally still clears the single-flight guard, but nothing catches or converts the error), skipping every other pending completion, every remaining non-completion kind, AND the profile-0 account sweep in _doDrain — on every one of the 5 wired drain triggers, forever, until the row is fixed out of band. This directly contradicts the code's own stated invariant quoted above.
recommendation: Wrap each _decodePayload call in its own try/catch (or catch FormatException specifically) so a bad payload is treated like any other per-row failure: logged, markAttempted (or immediately dead-lettered, since it can never succeed), and does not block sibling rows or other kinds.
acceptance_criteria: Regression test: insert one outbox row with a non-JSON-object payload (e.g. payload: 'null') alongside a valid row of a different kind; drain() must not throw, the valid row must still be pushed, and the bad row must be marked attempted without blocking siblings.
Same test repeated for a malformed completion-kind row.

corrections: The EH-2/EH-3 rule citation is only loosely accurate — the raw exception IS caught and logged one layer up in sync_orchestrator.dart (satisfying EH-3's catch/log requirement and EH-2's presentation-boundary requirement), so this is better framed as a reliability/per-row-isolation defect (violates the file's own stated invariant) than a strict EH-2/EH-3 hit. Recommend keeping P1 but noting the rule tag is approximate.
